help.title: About Projects
help.overview: A Project is the top-level container for a development. Every edifice, floor, unit, lead, reservation, sale, lease, story, budget-related unit cost, and construction record hangs off a project. Creating a project does not create buildings — you add those next. The project record itself is identity, marketing, and commercial defaults, not the physical building.

sections.title: What a project holds
items: Name (required) — how the development is labelled in the panel, public site, and emails.
Description — long copy for listings and the public project page.
Main image (required) — used on cards, the public site, and galleries. Without it you cannot create the project.
Image gallery, video gallery, extra media files — optional visual set for marketing.
Marketing booklet (PDF) — brochure operators and the public site can offer.
Magazine title, magazine description, magazine PDF — editorial block when you publish a magazine-style page.
Social links (name, URL, optional logo) — up to 20 links shown with the project.
Featured on homepage + featured sort order — which projects appear in the public homepage row and in which order (lower sort comes first).
Sale commission % and reservation commission % — starting rates inherited by later sales and reservations. A deal can still carry its own figures.
sections.body: There is no status machine on Project itself. Delivery and commercial status live on edifices, units, reservations, sales, and leases.

sections.title: On this page
items: Create a project — main image is required; name is required.
Search and filter the list; switch card view vs table view.
Open a card to edit marketing, media, featured flags, and commission defaults.
Row menu: open edifices already scoped to that project.
Delete is a soft delete. The project can be restored. Children (edifices, units, deals) are not created or destroyed automatically when you delete or restore.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: A project can exist with zero edifices. Inventory starts when you add buildings, then floors, then units.
Public-site pages (gallery, featured row, magazine, project detail) read these marketing fields. Unpublished or missing media simply does not show.
Commission rates on the project are defaults only. Changing them later does not rewrite historical sales or reservations.
Dashboard and Overview KPIs that mention “project” are aggregations of units and deals under that project, not fields stored here.

sections.title: What hangs off a project
items: Physical tree: Project → Edifice → Floor → Unit.
Sales pipeline: leads (optional project interest), inspections, modification requests, reservations, sales, commissions.
Contracts Hub is a registry of those commercial documents — it does not create a new document type.
Rentals: leases and rental payments (also via Rentals Hub).
Content: stories (marketing journal) and construction updates (site progress).
Costs: unit costs booked against units of this project. Quality: snags on those units.
sections.body: Those records are created on their own pages and only reference the project. Deleting a project does not cascade-delete them.

sections.title: Typical next step
items: Create the project with a clear name and main image.
Add edifices (each needs the project, address, investment value, main image).
Add floors on each edifice, then units on each floor (unit type, number, areas, price).
Then either publish marketing (featured, stories) or start commercial work (leads → reservations / sales, or leases).
